title: Focal Inverse Distance Transform Maps for Crowd Localization
mechanism: Regress a focal inverse distance transform map (sharp peak at each label, smooth fall-off) instead of a binary or Gaussian map, then read out by local-maximum detection.
adaptation: Crack-only extra regression head on the U-Net++ decoder with target 1/(d^(a d+b)+c), d = distance to nearest crack label skeleton pixel, so a 1 px label shift changes the target smoothly. Read-out: ridge NMS along predicted normal, draw at per-source width chosen on val (ARTS 1.5, CFVS/CSIR 1.75, BMRK 3, SDLE 3.25 px). 24-class CE head kept for all other classes.
min_experiment: E0 first (no GPU): skeletonise house-ensemble crack predictions on CV folds and redraw at width 1-4 px per source to measure IoU headroom. Then arm = PF + FIDT crack head (MSE + I-SSIM), two read-outs (ridge-drawn vs CE logit with FIDT as auxiliary); baseline = PF house, 5 seeds, clean-49 test + module-grouped 5-fold CV; metrics relF1@2, components >=20 px, crack IoU, E1 relF1@2. Kill if CV relF1@2 gain < 0.01 and E1 relF1@2 gain < 0.03.
evidence: R: SOTA crowd localisation on six crowd datasets and one vehicle set; more robust on negative and very dense scenes. No thin-line test.
prior_overlap: Partial: offset-tolerant CE (n.d.) and Skeleton Recall (wider, IoU worse) also tolerate shift, but neither changed the output to a regressed distance field with a ridge read-out. Open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Crack-only auxiliary head on the U-Net++ decoder; target from distance to the crack label skeleton (1.0 at 0 px, 0.5 at 1 px, 0 beyond 20 px), computed after augmentation; 24-class CE head unchanged. Team CPU pre-check: FIDT of a mask and its 1 px shift correlate at median 0.919 vs binary IoU 0.548. Optional read-out: ridge NMS then draw at per-source width.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm PF + FIDT aux (stacked with orientation, as T5 arm 4) vs PF, cv5v2 2 seeds x 5 folds; metric crack components >=20 px found and relF1@2, width ratio guard; kill if components +<0.02 and relF1@2 +<0.01, or strict crack IoU down >0.01.
